text:
Aminata sat in her quiet kitchen with the tablet on the table. Autumn had come, and her old winter coat no longer fit her. Last week she had ordered a new one online, but it came in size large and was far too big. She tapped the little microphone and said, "Swap coat."
The assistant opened her recent orders and found the coat. "Do you want a medium instead?" it asked. "Yes, medium," said Aminata. The assistant started an exchange, put a return label on the screen, and told her the courier would collect the big coat on Thursday. It also said the medium one would arrive in about five days.
Aminata smiled. She had not needed to call the shop or find her glasses to read the small print. She put the tablet down and went to make a cup of tea.

Li ran a small kitchen shop, and on Monday morning she had a video call with a supplier about a new blender. She said to her phone, "Please join my ten o'clock call and share my screen with the price list." The phone did both. It opened the call link, and a moment later the price list showed on the screen for everyone.
The supplier was polite and let her speak first. Halfway through, a customer walked into the shop and Li had to step away. "Pause the screen share for now," she said, and the assistant paused it.
When she came back she said, "Resume the share." The list appeared again and the supplier nodded. At the end of the call Li said, "Thanks, that's all. Stop sharing and leave the call." The assistant closed the call, and her phone went back to the sales sheet for the day.

Someone who is grilling dinner before a trip, with a large bag packed and a ticket bought in a sale, wants to know if the flight is late.
Is my flight late?
Any delay on flight 482?
Is it delayed by more than an hour?
Will the plane leave on time or later than planned?
how late is the Lisbon flight
Has my departure moved back by half an hour or more?
Is the wait twice as long as it was this morning?
Could you please check whether my flight to Rome is running behind schedule?
I'd like to know if I have more time than I thought before I need to be at the gate.

A contact is a small card in your phone with a person's name, number, address and birthday. People keep contacts so they do not have to remember every number. Most changes are small. A friend gets a new phone, so you say, "Change Sam's number to 555 0142." A cousin moves house, so you say, "Update Rosa's address." You can also add a note, like "Likes honey cake," to help you remember a gift. If the assistant finds two people with the same name, it asks which one, and you can point to the right one on the screen. Many people add a birthday to each card, because a friend will be glad you remembered the day. When someone is no longer in your life, you can simply say, "Delete that contact."

name: daily_agenda_maker
does: Writes a short agenda for a meeting, folds small topics together so the meeting stays short, and sends it to everyone before the daily check-in.
inputs: the meeting time, the list of topics, and who is invited, for example a team or a visiting artist
people say:
- Make a plan for tomorrow's meeting
- Can you put together what we will talk about at ten?
- I need a list of topics for our team call
- Write up the agenda and send it to everyone
- Draw up an outline for the call with the design team

Person: I'm busy with my polymer clay pots today. Please set a timer for them.
Assistant: Happy to. How many minutes should I set it for?
Person: The block of clay says they should bake for eleven minutes.
Assistant: Done. The timer is set for eleven minutes, and I will tell you when it ends.
Person: Lovely. Could you also paint the pots for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't paint. But I can remind you to paint them when they have cooled. Would you like that?
Person: Yes, remind me in one hour.
Assistant: Okay, I will remind you in one hour.

Person: need a new guest wifi pasword pls
Assistant: Of course. How long should it last, one day or one week?
Person: just today. a pair of clients are coming at two
Assistant: Done. The new password works until midnight, and the router will beep once when it is ready. Should I send it to your phone?
Person: yes. and tell me the exact speed too
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't run a speed test from here. I can send you the password now, though.
Person: ok thanks, send it
Assistant: Sent. It is on your phone.

Someone driving with a kid in the back on a dry day wants to know how long the trip will take, and whether another road is quicker.
How long is the drive?
Hang on, is there a faster way to get there?
What's the time to Gran's house?
Will we get there sooner if I take the back road?
How much longer until we arrive?
Is there a route that saves ten minutes?
Could you tell me if the other road is half as slow as this one?
I'd like to know how long the trip home will take, and if a quicker way exists.
Is traffic worse than usual, or will we be there in under an hour?

Laura stood at the stove with flour on her hands. A spider was walking along the window above the sink, but she had no time for it. The soup was cooked, the bread was nearly done, and her guests were coming at seven.
Her phone buzzed on the shelf. It was a missed call from her brother Marco. "Call Marco back," she said, "but not on speaker, the kitchen is too loud." The assistant dialled his number and kept the call quiet.
Marco did not answer. "Do you want to leave a voicemail?" asked the assistant.
"No voicemail," said Laura. "Just send him a text. Say I will call after dinner."
The assistant typed the words, read them back to her, and sent the text. Laura nodded and went back to her bread.

name: pick_up_where_left
does: Is a patient helper that finds the spot where a listener stopped in a podcast or audiobook and starts playing again from there.
inputs: the name of the show or book, such as a call-in radio show, a podcast about grilling, or a long novel
people say:
- Pick up my book where I left off
- Where did I stop in the history podcast?
- Keep going with the story from last night
- Play the rest of that episode
- Start the cooking show again from where it stopped

On a warm evening in June, Sara burned her finger on a hot oven tray. She was a retired teacher and she did not panic, but she did not want to guess either. She spoke to her tablet. "Excuse me, could you please tell me what to do for a small burn on my finger? I live alone, and I would like to be sure I do the right thing before I eat my dinner."
The assistant told her to hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes, and not to use ice or butter. It set a ten minute timer for her. When the timer rang, it asked if the skin was blistered. "No, just red," said Sara. The assistant said she could cover it with a clean, loose bandage. It also said to see a doctor if the pain got stronger. Sara thanked it and sat down to eat.

Dong-hyun was late for class and walked fast across the yard. He took out his phone and typed with his thumb, "wheres my order, i need it befor friday".
The assistant looked at his online orders. He had bought a big bag of baking sugar and a pair of cheap headphones. It said the sugar was out for delivery and would arrive by four o'clock. The headphones were stuck in a bad storm and would come on Thursday.
"Thursday is fine," Dong-hyun said to himself. "Chill, it's not a problem." Then he typed, "leave the sugar with the front desk". The assistant sent a note to the courier with that request and told him it was done.
Dong-hyun put his phone away and ran into class just as the bell rang.

Someone wants the air conditioning on and the house mild again by this evening.
Cool the house a bit
AC on, please
Can you make the living room cooler by seven tonight?
It's too hot in here
Please help me cool down the bedroom before bed on Friday evening
I want the whole house mild when I get home at six
Turn the fan on low until the afternoon
Could you set the air conditioning to come on tomorrow morning at eight?

name: dough_rise_timer
does: Sets a timer for rising dough, tells you when it is ready for the oven, and reminds you to paint the top with egg before baking, even if you can only give a rough guess of the room's warmth.
inputs: the kind of dough, how warm the kitchen is, and where it is resting, even if it is on a towel on the couch
people say:
- How long does my bread dough need to rise?
- Is the dough ready for the oven yet?
- Start a timer for the dough, it's a cold kitchen today
- Remind me when the pizza dough has doubled
- Tell me when to shape the loaves

A shopping list helps you remember what to buy so you do not stand in the shop and wonder. Most people keep it on their phone and tell the assistant what to put on it. They say "Add milk" or "We are out of eggs." Some people take a picture of the fridge, so they can see what is missing. Others ask the assistant to convert a recipe into a list, with each thing in one line. When the list changes, people say "Take bread off" or "Put two apples on." One family has a funny rule: anything that runs out goes on the list that same day. That way nobody opens an empty box of cereal on Monday morning.

Zofia had lived in the city for only a week. She came home and found a card on her door. It said a parcel was waiting at the post office, and nobody had been there to sign for it.
She sighed and spoke to her phone. "I'm never home when the courier comes, and I can't afford to lose this one. It's my winter coat."
The assistant understood. It showed her the nearest post office, which was ten minutes away and open until six. It said she could be back from work by half past five, in time to collect it. Then it asked, "Would you like to make a permanent change, so that parcels go to a pickup point near your office?"
"Yes, please," said Zofia. The assistant saved the new address and set a reminder to collect the coat at five thirty.

Silvia never liked her phone. One afternoon she came out of the shop with a heavy box in her arms and could not remember where she had parked. She stood in the car park and said, loudly, "Where is my car, and is the tyre pressure okay?"
The assistant answered both. The car was on level two, in row C, and the pressure was fine on three tyres, but the rear left was a little low. Silvia had guessed something was wrong, because the car pulled to one side that morning.
The assistant also said the car park charged hourly, and she had been there for two hours. "It will cost six euros," it said. Silvia thanked it, found her car, and put the box in the back. She drove to the garage to fill the tyre.

Sven woke up and rubbed his eyes. Last night a screw had fallen out of his bookshelf, and now one side hung crooked. He sat up on the edge of the bed and said to his phone, "Order the same screws as last time, but not the long ones. I don't want to drill any deeper."
The assistant looked at his last order and found a box of short wood screws. It added them to the basket and asked, "Should I send them to your home address?" Sven said yes.
The assistant placed the order and said it would arrive tomorrow. Then it offered to follow the delivery and tell him when the parcel was close. "Good idea," Sven mumbled, and fell back onto his pillow for ten more minutes.

Emi stood in the empty living room, surrounded by boxes. The wind rattled the window and the street outside was snowy and quiet. The kids zoomed down the hall with their toy cars while she held her phone.
"The movers come on Friday, and I don't think anyone has told the power company," she said.
The assistant understood that this was a request. It found the power company on her list and asked, "Do you want to stop the service at this address on Friday and start it at your new address?" Emi said yes and gave the new street.
The assistant sent the form, and a note appeared on the screen to say the change was booked. Emi put a tick on her list and picked up another box.

Person: It's too bright in the bedroom. I just got home from work.
Assistant: I can help. How dim should the lights be? They are at fifty percent now.
Person: Half of that, please.
Assistant: Done. The bedroom lights are at twenty-five percent.
Person: Thanks. I spent twelve hours on my feet. Could you turn off the kitchen light too? I think I left it on when I cooked last night.
Assistant: Yes, the kitchen light is off now.
Person: Now can you sweep the hall with the broom?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sweep. I only control the lights and the speakers. Would you like a reminder to sweep after you rest?
Person: Yes, tomorrow at noon.

Person: Excuse me, could you please remind me to call my mother on Sunday? I moved here last month and I keep forgetting, and I know she misses me.
Assistant: Of course. What time on Sunday should I remind you?
Person: Around six in the evening. She lives far to the east, so that is a good hour for her too.
Assistant: Okay. I will remind you on Sunday at six. What should I name the reminder?
Person: Please name it "Call Mom".
Assistant: Done. The reminder "Call Mom" is set for Sunday at six in the evening.

Person: Please find us a room in Lisbon for three nights.
Assistant: Sure. How many guests will there be, and which night do you arrive?
Person: Two adults and two kids. Sorry, make that three kids, I forgot my niece. We arrive on the ninth of May.
Assistant: Got it: two adults, three kids, one big family room, from the ninth of May. Shall I show the choices?
Person: Yes, but I can't click on the little buttons while I hold the baby. Can you read them out and turn the volume up? The kids are loud.
Assistant: The volume is up. The first room is a big family room with two beds and a sofa bed. It costs ninety euros a night.
Person: That sounds good. Take that one.

name: room_heating_plan
does: Sets, changes or cancels a heating plan for one room, so it is warm when people are at home.
inputs: which room, for example the south bedroom or the room with the sofa, the temperature you want, and the time
people say:
- Warm up the south bedroom by seven
- Keep the sofa room cozy tonight
- Stop the morning heat for tomorrow
- I'm cold, can you turn the radiator on in the hall?
- Don't heat the house while we're away this weekend

Mai was babysitting her little cousin, who had finally fallen asleep. It had taken an hour, and she felt as if she had won a game. She sat at the computer to finish her homework, with the baby monitor beside her.
She typed to her phone, "baby monitor is so quiet, i can barely hear anything".
The assistant understood what she meant. The monitor volume was at the minimum, so it raised the volume to a middle level and said, "I turned the monitor up. Can you hear the baby breathing now?"
"Yes, I can," Mai said. She also asked when the baby had last eaten. The assistant checked the feeding log and said it was at five o'clock, so the next feed would be around eight. Mai set a reminder and went back to her homework.

Odile got home at eight in the morning with her eyes burning from the bright lights at the hospital. She was a nurse, and she had been awake all night. Before she lay down, she spoke to the smart speaker on the shelf.
"Post in the neighborhood group that the garden sale is on the first of May," she said. "Then turn off my notifications until four this afternoon."
The assistant wrote the post and read it back: "Garden sale on the first of May. Come and say hello!" Odile said it was fine, and the assistant sent it to the group. Then it silenced the notifications from her social media apps until four.
"Thank you," Odile whispered. She pulled the curtains and slept without a single buzz from her phone.

Tunde woke up late. Rain drummed on the roof, and his clock said ten past eight. He grabbed his phone and mumbled two words, "Route to work?"
The assistant looked at the traffic. There was an accident on the main road, which meant a long wait. It offered a small road along the river instead. "That way takes twenty-five minutes," it said. "The main road takes fifty."
"River road," said Tunde. The assistant started the directions, and the phone read the first turn out loud while he pulled on his shoes. He ran to the car, still half asleep, and followed the quiet voice all the way to his office. He arrived five minutes before his first meeting.

Someone wants the dog fed now, in the tidy bowl by the front door, with a slice of apple on the side.
Feed the dog
Dinner time for Max
Max is staring at his empty bowl
It's past his usual dinner time, I think
Can you put out the dog's food now, please?
He has been walking around the kitchen for an hour
Please open the feeder so he can eat
I'd like the dog to have his dinner before we leave, if you could start it
My dog looks very hungry

name: pantry_stock_counter
does: Counts the cans, boxes and bottles in the pantry and the fridge, and lists what is running low, with a bigger check for the yearly clean-out, so you do not need a midnight trip to the shop.
inputs: the room or shelf to check, and the least amount of each thing you want to keep
people say:
- What are we running out of?
- How many eggs are left?
- Do we have any rice?
- Check the pantry before I go shopping
- Is the milk almost gone?

A focus timer helps you work hard for a short time and then rest. A common routine is twenty-five minutes of work and five minutes of break. The idea is to keep your mind fresh, so you do not stare at the screen for hours. People use the breaks to stand up, drink water, or charge their phone. Many people change the timer to fit them. They say, "Make the work part longer," "Shorten my break," or "Start a timer for forty minutes." Some people narrow their goal to one task, like "Focus on my report until noon." A traveler waiting at the airport can use the same routine to answer emails, one short block at a time.

Aarav, a retired teacher, was packing for a trip. His taxi was coming in a small amount of time, so he tidied the hall in a hurry and picked up his bag. He turned to the smart lock and said, "Lock the front door, but don't lock the garage. My son needs to get his tools this afternoon."
The assistant locked the front door and left the garage open. "Do you want me to close the garage later?" it asked.
"Yes, please," said Aarav. "Remind me at five to check it is closed."
The assistant set a reminder for five o'clock. Aarav heard the taxi horn outside, picked up his bag, and walked to the car. The door clicked behind him, locked and safe.

Many people forget birthdays, so they ask the assistant to keep the dates for them. You say, "Remember that my sister's birthday is on the third of June," and a few days before, the assistant reminds you. It can also help with gift ideas. If a friend loves to dance, you might ask, "What can I give someone who loves dance?" The assistant may suggest a class or a pair of good shoes. People change things all the time. They say, "Move the reminder to a week before," or "Sit down with me and write a card." Some people pick a card with a red ribbon, others choose a plain white one. Either way, the assistant helps the day feel easy.

Marisa ran a small cafe, and her pea soup was the most popular dish on the menu. Today a school group had booked lunch, and she needed to make the soup for forty people. Her recipe made only four bowls.
She wiped her hands and said to her phone, "My recipe makes four bowls. Make it enough for forty, and set a timer for twenty minutes so I remember to start the oven."
The assistant multiplied every amount by ten and read them out: ten cups of peas, five onions, and ten spoons of salt. Marisa also asked how much the extra peas would cost, but the assistant said it did not know the prices at her shop. It set the timer for twenty minutes.
Marisa nodded, took out her biggest pot, and added a purple cabbage salad to the day's menu.

Someone who booked a game night wants to know the score of a board game, where one sad player is far behind and the tiles are in a basket.
What's the score?
Who is winning?
How many points is Dan ahead?
Am I behind by more than ten?
Tell me everyone's totals
Is it close, or is someone way ahead?
How many more points do I need to catch up?
Could you please read out the score for each player, from the most points to the least?

Joost was unpacking boxes in his shop when he remembered his uncle's medicine. The nurse had said Uncle Piet should take his pills at noon and weigh himself every morning. Joost's hands were full of coat hangers, so he typed fast on his phone.
"remind my uncle to take his pils at noon and call me if he doesnt answer"
The assistant understood the whole message. At noon it spoke through the speaker in Uncle Piet's kitchen, in a friendly, personal way: "Time for your pills, Uncle Piet." Uncle Piet did not answer, so the assistant called Joost. Joost laughed and said, "He is in the garden again." He phoned his uncle's mobile himself. Uncle Piet picked up on the third ring, and the pills were taken ten minutes late.

Most people have a usual drink. It might be coffee with one sugar, or tea with a splash of milk. A machine or an assistant can make it the same way each morning, so you do not have to think about it. People often change how strong or sweet the drink is. They say, "Make it stronger," "Increase the sugar by one spoon," or "A little less milk, please." On a cold day they may ask for something fancy, like a latte with foam. In summer they may ask for an iced tea, poured from a can or made fresh. A good habit is to taste the drink first, and then tell the assistant what to change.

Person: Please call Anna.
Assistant: Which Anna? I have Anna Brown and Anna Lopez.
Person: Anna Brown. No, wait, I mean Anna Lopez, from the hotel.
Assistant: Calling Anna Lopez now.
Person: My glasses are foggy and I cannot read the screen. Did anyone call me this morning?
Assistant: Yes, there were two missed calls. One was from your son, and one from the doctor's office. Shall I read the voicemail?
Person: Yes, the one from my son. The phone flashed, but I did not hear it ring.
Assistant: Playing it now.

Kenji had ten minutes before his train and his bag was already on his shoulder. He called out to the speaker, "Set the pool to twenty-eight degrees by this evening."
"Should I start the heater now?" asked the assistant.
"No, at four o'clock," said Kenji. "Not before."
The assistant set the heater for four. Then it scanned the pool sensors and said, "The pump battery is low, but everything else is working well. The water is twenty-three degrees now."
"Thanks," said Kenji. "Remind me to change the battery tomorrow." The assistant made a note, and Kenji ran out of the door just as the train began to roll into the station.

Dana walked out of the hospital after a long night shift and put her earbuds in. The coffee in her bag was stale, and all she wanted was a shower. She spoke to her phone in a low voice.
"text mom im on my way home, wil have breakfast there"
The assistant turned her words into a message and read it back: "Mom, I'm on my way home, will have breakfast there." Dana nodded, and the assistant sent it.
A moment later her mom replied that she was making pancakes. The assistant read the answer into her earbuds. Dana smiled, asked it to shift her alarm for the afternoon to four o'clock, and walked slowly to the bus stop.

Zoe stood at the front of the meeting room, under the big tv. She had to update the numbers for the sales sheet, and her head was full of figures. She spoke to her phone.
"Add up one hundred twenty, eighty and forty-five, and tell me if that is more than two hundred fifty."
The assistant said the total was two hundred forty-five. "That is five less than two hundred fifty," it added.
Zoe nodded. "Now take half of it." The assistant answered one hundred twenty-two and a half. Zoe typed the numbers into the sheet, checked them once on the screen, and pressed save. The meeting started two minutes later, and the sheet was ready.

Person: book a tabel for tonight
Assistant: Happy to. For how many people, and at what time?
Person: 4 at 7. nothing too pricey, i can't afford a fancy place
Assistant: Understood. What kind of food would you like?
Person: anything with deep dish pizza
Assistant: There is a pizza place five minutes from your office with a table for four at seven. Shall I book it?
Person: yes please. also is there a hardware shop open near there? my chair has a loose screw
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't search for shops. I can only help with restaurants. Your table is booked.

Taras closed his shop for the night and sat on the couch with a bowl of pea soup. He was tired and wanted something simple to watch. He lifted his phone and said, "Movies nearby?"
The assistant listed three films at the cinema around the corner, with times. One was a comedy at eight. "The comedy," said Taras.
The assistant showed the trailer and asked if he wanted to buy a ticket. "Not yet," said Taras. "First, connect to the living room tv." The assistant connected the phone to the tv, and the trailer played on the big screen. Taras laughed twice, then said, "Buy one ticket." The assistant did it, and Taras finished his soup.

Camille was proud of the new painting in her hall. It was a perfect spring day, and the garden had begun to grow. She did not like technology, but her son had put a smart lock on the front door and told her to just talk to it.
Before she left for the market, she said, "Is my front door locked? I think I left it open longer than usual this week."
The assistant said the door had been unlocked for almost two hours, which was twice as long as usual. "Do you want me to lock it now?" it asked.
"Yes, please," said Camille. The lock clicked. She smiled, picked up her basket, and walked down the street with a lighter heart.

Person: I just got home from work and my brain is mush. My sister's birthday is on Saturday.
Assistant: Would you like some gift ideas, or a reminder?
Person: Ideas, please. She has dreamed of a garden for years, but she only has the flat upstairs from mine.
Assistant: A window box with herb seeds would be a nice gift. How much would you like to spend?
Person: Not sure. Maybe twenty euros?
Assistant: That is enough for a long box, soil and three kinds of seeds. Shall I remind you to buy it?
Person: Yes, tomorrow at five. I'll park by the garden store on my way home.

Someone excited about a dinner party wants to scale a recipe up for twelve people, so the meal will shine, and they can't nail the maths alone.
Make this recipe for twelve
Double it, and tell me the new amounts
Scale the cake to eight slices and list the cups and spoons
I need this soup to feed twelve, so change the amounts and the number of servings
Cut it in half and tell me how many it serves
Can you make it bigger, and write the new list in cups?
Please turn this recipe into one for six, and read the amounts out loud
I'd like to triple the sauce and also know how many people it will feed

Someone wants a plan for what to cook this week, with a good balance of foods, after a snowy weekend of eating badly and wanting to practice cooking at home more.
What should I cook this week?
Plan my dinners for the week
Give me five healthy dinners
The fridge is empty and I'm tired of takeout
I don't know what to eat all week
Could you make a menu for seven days with fish, beans and vegetables?
It's freezing outside and I want warm food every night
I'd like a simple plan for packed lunches too, if that's not too much trouble

Edward sat by his pool on a warm day. The sun was shining in a clear sky, and the water looked a little cold. He was a grandparent now, and his grandchildren were coming to swim in the afternoon. He lifted his phone and said, "Pool temperature?"
The assistant answered, "The water is twenty degrees."
"Warmer," said Edward.
The assistant asked how warm he wanted it. "Twenty-six," he said. The assistant turned on the electric heater and said it would take about three hours. Edward sat back with his book. When the children arrived, the water was just right, and the little ones jumped in with a happy shout.

Isaac sat on the sofa with a cup of coffee that tasted cold. His kids were asleep, and the pale glow of the tablet screen hurt his eyes. He had been working late all week and wanted one quiet night.
"Turn on a blue light filter, and put the phone on do not disturb until Friday morning," he said.
The assistant made the screen warmer and dimmer. Then it silenced the calls and messages. "Only calls from your family will come through," it said. "Is that all right?"
"Yes, thank you," said Isaac. He finished his coffee, went upstairs, and slept for nine hours without a single beep.

Paolo stared out the airport window. It was snowing hard, and the silver planes sat very still on the ground. He had his boarding card in one hand and his coffee in the other. The big board above him showed no new news.
He took out his phone. "Gate number?" he asked.
The assistant looked at his flight. "Gate fourteen," it said. "But your flight is delayed by forty minutes, because of the snow."
Paolo sighed. "Tell me when it changes." The assistant said it would. Forty minutes later his phone buzzed, and a message said boarding had begun. Paolo threw his cup in the bin and walked to gate fourteen.

Femke's baby slept badly because the nursery felt stuffy. It was spring, and the pollen was high. She held the baby with one arm and said to the speaker, "Is the air in the nursery okay?"
The assistant answered that the air was dusty and dry. "Would you like me to start the purifier?" it asked.
"Yes, and turn it on every night at eight," said Femke. "Make that a permanent schedule."
The assistant set it up. Then Femke said, "Remind me in two weeks to change the filter." The assistant made a note. Femke later put the old filter in the recycling, and the nursery smelled fresh again.

Putri was minding her shop when she remembered her son's school project. She grabbed her phone and typed fast.
"remind jonas to water his bean plant, it is next to the radiator, project due thrusday"
The assistant read the message and understood it. It sent a note to Jonas's tablet that said, "Please water your bean plant today. The project is due on Thursday." It also set a second reminder for Wednesday evening.
That night Jonas wrote back, "The beans are very funny, one is taller than the rest!" Putri laughed and showed the message to her customers. The assistant saved the due date in her calendar.
